# Original Gemma protocol and runtime contract

Generated by `tools/generate_ai_maaiveld_fixtures.py` from the original
`ai_maaiveld.py` and `vllm_runtime.py`, without application, settings or account
initialization. HTTP, process launch and scene rendering are captured fakes.

The reference contains eight parser cases, the exact Dutch prompt and chat
request fields, two numbered-map bounds/aspect layouts, and two runtime command
and environment cases. PNG compression is not compared; the data URL carries
the same image pixels. Model text remains a suggestion for explicit review.

Additional native tests use localhost fake HTTP responses, stalled-response
cancellation and short-lived hidden system processes. They never launch vLLM,
initialize a GPU, install packages or download a model. Runtime tests cover
existing-process reuse after readiness timeouts, restart after exit, cancellation
of a new launch, Windows environment casing and local DLL preparation.

On Windows, owned executable startup uses documented `CreateProcessW` with
`CREATE_SUSPENDED`, a non-inheritable Job Object with
`JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, assignment before `ResumeThread`, and an
explicit stdin/log handle list. No breakaway or uncontained fallback is allowed.
An incompatible enclosing CI Job Object fails closed before application code
runs. Only handles returned from this owned launch are terminated; external
ready servers and externally configured endpoints never enter the owned job.

Native Rust child/grandchild fixtures verify startup cancellation, owner drop,
cleanup after the root executable has already exited, failed assignment before
child code runs, and survival of an unrelated fixture process. These fixtures
never launch vLLM, GPU workers or model downloads. The current Windows test host
supports the nested-job assignment; real GPU/runtime acceptance remains separate.

Windows API contract: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects
